messages.subject: Reshape summary table output
parts:
Been struggling a bit with something I'm trying to do with reshape -
I'm a newbie to R so the learning curve is steep - and your help would
be appreciated.

If I cast a dataframe and write it to a table - when there are 'NAs'
they appear before any aggregated rows like so

write.table(pivottable, file='/tmp/mylist.txt', sep="|",
row.names=FALSE)

The NAs are valid - in the output below the sales values are sorted by
product_group within account. There are obviously some rows in the
data frame where there is no product_group (unknown, uncategorized or
missing data, I guess). Reshape correctly includes the NA labeled sale
value in the sub-total for, say 'Sales other' but outputs it BELOW
that sub-total. I've snipped the output for just the "Sales Other"
account

2010 was 32.50. I think it should look like this

>> "account"|"group_desc"|"2009_value"|"2010_value"
"Sales Other"|"PR C"|0|32.5
"Sales Other"|NA|2967.12|0
"Sales Other"|"(all)"|2967.12|32.5

i.e. the NA is above the subtotal.

parts:
Hi again Martyn -

I would go through with a ddply, check if any entries in group_desc are NA, and if they are exchange the last two rows.  So something like

# making fake data, you could send to me with dput()... :)
data <- data.frame(
  account = rep(letters[1:5], each = 5),
  group_desc = rep(c(letters[23:26],'(all)'), 5),
  value = rpois(25, lambda = 1000)
)
data$group_desc[c(3,8,11)] <- NA
data <- ddply(data, .(account), function(df){
  df$value[5] <- sum(df$value[1:4])
  df <- df[order(df$group_desc, decreasing = TRUE),]
  df
})


# now for the fix...
data <- ddply(data, .(account), function(df){
  n <- nrow(df)
  if(any(is.na(df$group_desc))){
    df[(n-1):n,] <- df[n:(n-1),]
  }
  df
})

Hope it helps,
david.

Sure. :)

This also works in the same example I sent you, using factor levels instead of ddply :

# fix 2...
data <- within(data,{
  group_desc <- as.character(group_desc)
  group_desc[is.na(group_desc)] <- 'NA'
  group_desc <- factor(group_desc, levels = c('w','x','y','z','NA','(all)'))
})
data <- arrange(data, account, group_desc)

Is that easier?  Most of the code here is used just to fix the fact that R deals with missing values (NA) differently than other types (numeric, character, logical, etc.).  The underlying idea is just to put a different order on the set 'w', ..., '(all)' and then sort by that new order.  Perhaps you will find this article helpful : http://wiki.had.co.nz/data-structures.

Cheers
david.

On Fri, Jan 7, 2011 at 10:16 AM, David Kahle <david.ka...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi again Martyn -
I would go through with a ddply, check if any entries in group_desc are NA,
and if they are exchange the last two rows.  So something like
# making fake data, you could send to me with dput()... :)
data <- data.frame(
  account = rep(letters[1:5], each = 5),
  group_desc = rep(c(letters[23:26],'(all)'), 5),
  value = rpois(25, lambda = 1000)
)
data$group_desc[c(3,8,11)] <- NA
data <- ddply(data, .(account), function(df){
  df$value[5] <- sum(df$value[1:4])
  df <- df[order(df$group_desc, decreasing = TRUE),]
  df
})

# now for the fix...
data <- ddply(data, .(account), function(df){
  n <- nrow(df)
  if(any(is.na(df$group_desc))){
    df[(n-1):n,] <- df[n:(n-1),]
  }
  df
})
Hope it helps,
david.

David

OK - actually this is a little easier to read and decipher for me!!
Looking back at the previous fix I can see they are doing pretty much
the same thing, i.e. resorting the result from the cast operation. And
I 'get' this now and can see how it works, but... (there's always a
but!)

What I'm ultimately trying to do is get data from a postgresql db and
via melt/cast to produce a pivot table like report for web display by
dumping the result of the melt/cast to a pipe delimited file. The R
'bit' will be called from within the PHP app I've built via the PL/R
postgreSQL language extension. The reshape melt function will be
passed an SQL query as a dataframe and the cast will be based on
parameters passed at runtime from PHP via PL/R. The SQL that produces
the dataframe for the melt part will have outer joins - almost
guaranteeing NULLS and therefore <NA> in the result set. So....

1. I don't know where the <NA>s will be (i.e. which columns or rows)
2. The pivot formula is constructed at runtime so I don't know
anything about the rows/columns in the dataframe returned until
runtime.

The result I posted to you is great and 'SO' close apart from this one
little gotcha - i.e. the <NA>s not seeming to appear in the 'right'
order. As a test I threw the same query at an OOo datapilot (took
ages!) and the NULLs appeared first!

BTW - thanks so much for the responses - the help here is fantastic.

Martyn

This is fixed in the development version of reshape and plyr, but
until those are released you can do something like:

fixlevels <- function(x) {
if (!is.factor(x)) return(x)

levs <- levels(x)
if (!any(c("(all)", NA) %in% levs)) return(x)

others <- setdiff(levs, c("(all)", NA))
factor(x, levels = c(others, NA, "(all)"), exclude = NULL)
}

mydf[] <- lapply(mydf, fixlevels)

Hadley
